html:
The Kuyani are an Aboriginal people of South Australia, in dry country west of the Flinders Ranges, between Lake Torrens and the ranges, north of present day Port Augusta.

Their neighbours were the Adnyamathanha in the ranges, the Arabana to the north, the Kokatha to the west and the Nukunu and Barngarla to the south. Their country lay on old trade routes that carried red ochre and other goods across the continent.

Sheep runs reached the area from the 1850s. The map shows the Kuyani from 1600 to 1800. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Kuyani are an Aboriginal people of South Australia, in dry country west of the Flinders Ranges, between Lake Torrens and the ranges, north of present day Port Augusta.
